item.title: Twin Health uses AI to build metabolic digital twins for patients
item.description:
Twin Health uses AI to build metabolic digital twins for patients

Digital twins are a new concept in health where a virtual model of a person is created using various data points, including lab results, wearable data, images, and genetic profiles. Twin Health is a program designed to help users manage their metabolism, weight, and conditions like diabetes by creating an AI-powered, color-coded food database that predicts how a user’s glucose levels will react to specific dietary choices.

🧩 How it works

  • The system consumes daily metabolic data, including body composition from smart scales and blood pressure readings.
  • Users integrate data from continuous glucose monitors (CGMs) and wearable devices to feed the model.
  • The AI generates insights based on how the body reacts to food intake, which helps refine the accuracy of the twin over time.
  • Clinicians can test how a patient might react to specific medicines or treatments by running simulations on their digital twin.

⚙️ Key details

  • Building a digital twin requires an extensive collection of personal data over a 90-day period.
  • Users participate in check-ins with human coaches and doctors to review lab results and monitor progress.
  • The service is currently experimental and not available for widespread download.
  • Common feedback from users includes reports of tracking fatigue.

💡 Why it matters

  • Theoretically, digital twins can help healthcare providers assess injury risks.
  • The technology aims to predict disease progression.
  • It supports the implementation of preventive care while aiming to minimize adverse effects for patients.

#DigitalTwin #HealthTech #AI #MetabolicHealth #Wearables

Source: My AI doppelganger tells me what to eat

item.title: Streamlined Edge ML Workflow for WeBe Band Wearable Device
item.description:
Streamlined Edge ML Workflow for WeBe Band Wearable Device

Researchers have developed a streamlined edge ML workflow to enable the rapid development, optimization, and deployment of machine-learning models directly on the WeBe Band, a wrist-worn device for multimodal physiological data monitoring.

🧩 How it works

The system focuses on system-level automation and deployability, integrating the open-source Piccolo AI ecosystem with an automated pipeline. This framework provides the following capabilities:

  • Hardware-aware model compilation
  • Generation of deployable firmware artifacts
  • Support for over-the-air (OTA) deployment
  • Hardware-aware quantization and AutoML
  • Performance profiling to meet latency targets within device memory and power limitations

⚙️ Key details

The workflow supports multiple lightweight model classes and provides on-device profiling tools to evaluate memory footprint and inference latency under realistic conditions.

Model Class Performance Observations
Classical machine-learning algorithms Offer strong real-time performance
Neural networks Require careful resource management

💡 Why it matters

This work enables researchers and developers to rapidly iterate on models and evaluate them directly on target hardware. While demonstrated on the WeBe Band platform, the workflow is designed to be extensible to other ML-powered edge devices.

#EdgeML #Wearables #AutoML #EmbeddedSystems

Source: A Rapid Pipeline for Training and Deploying ML Models on WeBe Band
